summary: A 10-foot wooden L-4 lookout on Indian Butte in the Deschutes National Forest, built in 1932 and now gone; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 10-foot wooden tower
facts.status_note: The tower is gone. Neither the register nor firelookout.com gives a removal date.

corrections.why: 21.3 m is about 70 ft. The register and firelookout.com give a 10-foot tower, and the federal survey description quoted on the Forest Lookouts page says the structure is 10 feet high.
Spacing typo in the record; the register itself has the same missing space.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A standard house was planned in 1930 and a fireman was to be lookout in 1931; the 1932 date in the register and firelookout.com is when the tower was built.

sources.title: Indian Butte Lookout Site, Former Fire Lookout Sites Register

notes_for_editor: Record height 21.3 m (about 70 ft) is contradicted by three sources giving 10 ft; corrected to 3.0 m. Removal date unknown; no source gives one. Newspapers of 1924 to 1931 call the summit Indian Spring(s) Butte; identity with Indian Butte is assumed, not verified. The 2006 register photo shows the site but its caption does not describe remains. Search results for the removal date turned up only map entries and a Deschutes disposal listing that does not include Indian Butte.
